judged_text: createEvent selects the calendar via find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId) with a 'primary' fallback, so a destinationCalendar row with a null credentialId — exactly the case EventManager routes through its else branch — has its externalId silently ignored. Users whose destinationCalendar rows have no credentialId get their bookings created on the Google primary calendar instead of the destination calendar they configured (the old code used destinationCalendar.externalId), and the stored reference carries no externalCalendarId, so the event is also unaddressable for later update/delete.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the target calendar is now chosen only via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, with fallback `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. If a `destinationCalendar` entry has no `credentialId`, this `find` returns `undefined` and Google inserts into `primary`, ignoring any configured `externalId` that might exist on that destination row (old code used `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly). This situation is reachable via `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`: when `destination.credentialId` is falsy, it goes through the `else` branch and calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing `destination.externalId`, so `CalendarManager.createEvent` returns an `EventResult` with `externalId` unset. Later, `EventManager` uses `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`, so the stored reference can lack an `externalCalendarId`, making update/delete unable to target the non-primary calendar.
